notes.summary: Independent quotient/nonalgebraization proof under named published foundations; bounded ordinary psh potentials separate all analytic points and give dense continuous tests.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs the specified proper smooth strict analytic surface over C((s)), excludes separated finite-type algebraic-space algebraizations using disc/circle Picard triviality, annulus filling, Laurent multiplier recurrence and analytic regularity, and fixes a degenerate positive datum of raw mass two. Proves point separation and vector-lattice density without global strict positivity. Deeper named analytic foundations remain conventional published inputs, not newly recursively audited.
notes.text:
This is an independent proof draft relative to the conventional published foundations stated below. No supplied note or positive verdict is a premise. Put K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, Y=(G_m^2)^an and Λ=⟨(t,2),(3,t)⟩. On Y let x_i=-log|z_i|. Then Λ translates x by Z². Let X=Y/Λ.

The retained analytic foundations are Conrad–Temkin, Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces, https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/analgpaper.pdf. Lemma 4.2.3 constructs an analytic quotient of an étale equivalence relation when its restrictions to an ordinary open cover have quotients; these local quotients are open subspaces covering the quotient. Lemma 4.2.4 identifies coherent G-sheaves with coherent descent data for a flat quasi-finite analytic surjection. Its proof reduces locally to finite faithfully flat affinoid algebras, where completed tensor products are ordinary tensor products. Closed immersions descend through their coherent ideals. Theorem 2.3.1 reflects separatedness and smoothness under analytification, and properness for finite-type maps; Example 2.3.2 compares algebraic and analytic stalks at closed points. The applied statements and complete immediate arguments were read in retained primary extracts. Deeper Berkovich descent remains a conventional foundation.

Inverse images of tropical rectangles of coordinate widths less than one have disjoint nonidentity translates and furnish ordinary open quotient charts. On bounded tropical ranges the relation is a finite union of disjoint closed deck graphs. The compact fundamental polyannulus x⁻¹([0,1]²) surjects onto X. A finite cover of this square by injective charts gives a flat quasi-finite surjection onto X with finite fibres; the product cover has the same properties. Relation ideals satisfy the deck cocycle, so coherent descent proves that the quotient diagonal is closed. This does not apply quasi-finite descent to the infinite-sheeted map Y→X. Rectangles with endpoints in (1/8)Z and nested widths below one give strict affinoid neighbourhoods. Consequently X is compact Hausdorff, separated, good, strict, smooth, pure two-dimensional, boundaryless and proper. Connectedness follows from the connected nested Laurent polyannuli covering Y and surjectivity of Y→X.

Here is the independent nonalgebraization argument. Gruson, Fibres vectoriels sur un polydisque ultramétrique (1968), IV.5 Theorem 1, applies to finite completed tensor products of disc algebras with radii in the divisible valuation group and unit-circle algebras. It gives SK⁰(H)=0; SK¹(H)=0 is unused. A rank-one projective module has the class of H, so stable equality followed by determinants trivializes it. Wide annuli are not inputs to this theorem. For a line bundle on A(r,R)×Z, trivialize its restriction to C(r)×Z and glue to the trivial bundle on D(r)×Z. The finite rational cover D(r)∪A(r,R)=D(R) has intersection C(r). Induction on the number of wide factors trivializes the glued bundle on D(R)×Z and hence the original bundle. The gluing input is Tate–Kiehl coherence as stated in Van der Put, Rigid analytic spaces (1975–76), 2.14–2.16.3: coherence is local on finite affinoid covers, affinoid coherent sheaves are finite modules with vanishing higher cohomology, and the stated descent equalizer applies. The complete relevant text and J7-09 diagram were read, including its explicit appeal to Kiehl. Thus Pic(P_m)=0 for P_m={|s|^m≤|z_i|≤|s|^(-m)}.

Compatibility on the noncompact torus requires an additional argument. If b=Σb_βz^β is a unit on P_m, its Gauss log norm is convex, and the inverse has the opposite convex norm. Therefore that norm is affine. A monomial maximizing it at an interior point agrees with the affine norm throughout the box. For its exponent α this yields
|b_β/b_α| exp((m/8)|β-α|₁)≤1.
Hence b=b_αz^α(1+g), with zero constant coefficient and ||g||_{P_j}≤|s|^(m-j) for j<m. A global unit on Y is a scalar monomial, since any different exponent would dominate along a tropical ray. Normalize successive trivializing frames by scalar monomials, obtaining e_{m+1}=(1+g_m)e_m on P_m. On fixed P_j, the products p_j=∏_{m=j}^∞(1+g_m) converge to units: the first finitely many factors are units, and the tails and inverse tails converge by the displayed estimate. The frames e_jp_j agree on overlaps and glue on the interior exhaustion. Thus Pic(Y)=0.

An equivariant line-bundle frame has scalar-monomial multipliers c_i z^{h_i}. Write h₁=(A,B), h₂=(C,D). Commutativity gives t^C2^D=3^At^B, hence C=B and A=D=0. Thus h₁=(0,k), h₂=(k,0). For k≠0 take λ=λ₁λ₂^{sign k} and h=(k sign k,k), so Q=v(λ^h)=2|k|>0. A section satisfying f(λz)=cz^hf(z) has Laurent coefficients
 a_{m+jh}=a_m c^j λ^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2).
Their valuations have leading term -Qj²/2, contradicting Laurent convergence on the unit polyannulus. For k=0, two nonzero exponents must have identical pairings with both period valuations and therefore coincide. Every nonzero equivariant section is then a single nowhere-vanishing monomial; two sections with the same multipliers are proportional.

For a meromorphic fraction F=g/h on the smooth torus, the pole ideal J={b:bF∈O} is the coherent kernel of multiplication by g into O/(h). Cancellation in regular local rings makes J principal of rank one. Stacks Tag 0AG0 states that regular local rings are UFDs; its complete induction proof was read. Flat analytic restrictions commute with this kernel and glue J. The regularity foundations are Ducros, Families of Berkovich spaces, 2.1.3(2),(5), asserting regularity of affinoid-domain and analytic-local restriction maps, and 2.1.4, asserting regularity of algebraic-to-analytic local maps for schemes locally of finite type over an affinoid algebra. Their deeper cited proofs are disclosed conventional inputs. A global frame of J on Y gives holomorphic f₀ and f₁=Ff₀ with the same deck multipliers. The preceding recurrence forces F to be constant. Hence Γ(X,M_X)=K.

If X=Z^an for a separated finite-type K-algebraic space, reflection makes Z smooth and proper of dimension two. It is connected and integral, since regularity separates its finitely many irreducible components. Stacks Tags 086U, 0BB1, 0EN6, 0ENA and 0END give a dense scheme locus and Γ(Z,K_Z)=K(Z), of transcendence degree two. The relevant hypotheses are decency, finitely many irreducible components on quasi-compact étale charts, weak associates of codimension zero, and field-monomorphism generic points for 0ENA; smooth separated finite-type Z satisfies them. Exact statements and immediate proofs were read. Regular algebraic-to-analytic local maps preserve nonzerodivisors, so local fractions analytify and descend. A closed point in a scheme open avoiding numerator and denominator zeros detects a nonzero rational function. Thus K(Z) injects into Γ(X,M_X)=K, a contradiction. This excludes separated finite-type algebraic-space algebraizations over the specified K. No assertion after every field extension is made.

Put ρ=|x|²/2 and θ=DDρ, where DD=d′d″. Deck changes of ρ are smooth affine functions, so θ descends as an ordinary smooth positive closed form with local smooth psh potentials. The CLD identity-torus calibrated integration convention has saturated lattice Z², degree one, and measure 2 det(Hess F) dx for smooth convex F, supported on the Gauss section. Applied to ρ and the unit fundamental square, it gives θ²=2i_*dx and raw mass M=2. Calibrated integration is a conventional published foundation; its factor 2!=2 is retained.

Let P be the minimal continuous psh sheaf of CLD Definition 8.1.7, closed under local uniform limits, and C={u∈C(X):ρ+u∈P locally}. Convex/max closure follows by two minimal-sheaf arguments. Convex combinations of smooth psh weights are psh and their smooth convex soft maxima converge uniformly to their maximum. Fixing one smooth weight, the other weights for which either operation belongs to P form a sheaf closed under uniform limits and containing smooth weights. Minimality gives every weight. Fix such a weight and repeat in the other slot. Thus the operations preserve P and C; constants belong to C.

C separates all analytic points. Different tropical classes are separated by a small smooth periodic εf(x) with I+ε Hess f≥0. For points in one tropical fibre, lift their coordinate to a and choose a chart |x_i-a_i|<r<1/2. Distinct seminorms differ on a Laurent polynomial P. Label them with |P(p)|>|P(q)| and put b=log|P(p)|. Let L bound log|P| on the closed polyannulus. Choose 0<δ<r²/4 and ε>0 with δ+ε(L-b)<r²/2. Set
 F=max(ρ_a,δ+ε(log|P|-b)), ρ_a=|x-a|²/2, u=F-ρ_a.
The strict boundary inequality gives a tropical collar where u=0, so extension by zero is continuous. Near a zero of P, F=ρ_a on an ordinary neighbourhood. Elsewhere soft maxima of two ordinary smooth psh weights approximate F locally uniformly. Hence u belongs even to the first approximation stage, without identifying that stage with all P. It satisfies u(p)=δ>u(q).

D=span_R C is a vector lattice. Convexity writes its members as A(p-q), p,q∈C. For common A>0,
 max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-2A(q+s)/2.
Minima follow by negation. For continuous h and η>0, separation and constants give f_xy∈D agreeing with h at x,y. At fixed x, finitely many sets {f_xy>h-η} cover X; their maximum g_x lies above h-η everywhere and equals h at x. Finitely many neighbourhoods where g_x<h+η cover X. Their minimum approximates h uniformly within η. Thus D is dense in all C(X), including off-skeleton tests.

There is no global strictness assertion. On the residue bidisc |z_i-1|<1, x_i=0 and θ=0. Curvature in the moments z_i-1 cannot be bounded by a multiple of θ there. Later strictness estimates use other bounded potentials.

notes.summary: Independent all-stage bounded Green/energy calculus and canonical generated energy for every bounded continuous decreasing presentation.
notes.detailedSummary: Checks corrected CLD applications, reconstructs fixed-current Hilbert gradients and cutoff closure for the entire minimal continuous sheaf, and proves bounded products, variation, cocycle, concavity and comparison. Proves presentation independence, simplex polynomial energy and finite-dual integrability. Decreasing generated energy continuity requires an already generated limit; intrinsic recognition, compactness and net flattening are not inferred.
notes.text:
Use the actual surface and datum of n1. The class is the ordinary all-stage minimal continuous sheaf P, without assuming equality with one smooth-approximation stage.

The applied CLD v2 foundations, arXiv:1204.6277v2, are Definition 8.1.7 and Lemma 8.1.8 for the minimal continuous sheaf and transfinite uniform closure; Lemma 8.5.1 for f_jT_j→fT under locally uniform continuous-coefficient convergence and weak positive-current convergence; Lemma 8.5.3 for smooth closed-factor differentiation; Lemma 8.5.5 for positivity and closedness of DD(fT) when f is continuous psh and T positive closed; 8.7.1, Propositions 8.7.2 and 8.7.4 for symmetric recursive products and local uniform continuity; and 8.8.4–5 for multilinear continuous-dpsh extension and smooth DD-null changes of potential. Proposition 7.2.8 identifies positive top currents with Radon measures on locally differentially separated spaces; 7.2.11–12 provide smooth-factor measures and continuous multiplication. Proposition 5.11.1 gives compact-support Stokes/Green, with boundary terms. Theorem 15.7.1 gives calibrated tropical calculus on separated pure-dimensional analytic spaces with their analytic boundary. By n1 the hypotheses hold and boundary terms on X vanish.

All these statements and complete immediate proofs were read in the corrected literal-LF units. Smooth cutoffs, partitions, scalar density, calibrated integration and underlying positivity remain conventional published foundations. In surface degree (1,1) only the positive-semidefinite matrix cone and scalar domination are used. General higher-degree strong-cone order-unit claims, arbitrary continuous-multiplier closedness from 8.6.7, and equality P=C₁ are not premises.

For u,v∈C put θ_u=θ+DD[u] and B(u,v)=θ∧θ_v+DD(uθ_v), MA(u)=B(u,u). Locally this is the actual recursive product of continuous psh weights. It is symmetric, positive and local, and affine changes of potential glue it. Testing exact terms by 1 gives B(u,v)(X)=M=2. Convex/max closure holds at all stages by n1.

Here is the additional Green proof. Fix a positive closed (1,1) current T. Complete compact smooth (1,0) forms modulo the null space of ∫a∧Jb∧T. Symmetry and positivity give a Hilbert pairing and Cauchy–Schwarz. Use local seminorms Q_{T,χ}(f,g)=∫χ d′f∧d″g∧T for nonnegative compact smooth cutoffs. Let H_T be the continuous functions locally uniformly approximable by smooth functions with strongly convergent gradients in these seminorms. Finite smooth partitions patch approximations: gradients of Σχ_i f_{i,k} are Σχ_i d′f_{i,k}+Σf_{i,k}d′χ_i. Both sums converge strongly, by gradient and uniform convergence respectively. Products and cutoffs obey the same argument. Continuous bounded coefficients act in the completion by smooth scalar approximation and ||fa||≤||f||∞||a||.

Gradients are unique. If f_k→0 uniformly and their gradients converge strongly to a, closedness gives ∫d′f_k∧Jb∧T=-∫f_k d′(Jb)∧T→0 for every compact smooth b. The right pairing is a finite signed measure. Density of smooth forms in the completion gives a=0. Cutoffs on larger patches give the local version.

If f∈H_T and L_Tf=DD(fT) is signed Radon, then ∫g L_Tf=-Q_T(f,g) for compactly supported g∈H_T. First prove this for smooth g by approximating f; then approximate g uniformly and strongly with fixed compact cutoff. Consequently
 Q_{T,χ}(w,w)=½∫w² DDχ∧T-∫χw L_Tw.
The sheaf of f∈H_T with L_Tf≥0 contains smooth psh functions. For a uniformly convergent sequence f_j choose nested cutoffs χ,η inside its uniform-convergence neighbourhood, η=1 near supp χ, and |f_j|≤B on the whole supp η. With ε=||f_j-f_k|| there,
 0≤Q_{T,χ}(f_j-f_k,f_j-f_k)
 ≤(ε²/2)||DDχ∧T||TV+2Bε||χ||∞||DDη∧T||TV.
Positivity bounds the mass of the two Laplacians by 2B||χ||∞||DDη∧T||TV. Thus gradients are strongly Cauchy. On each smaller patch choose smooth approximants with uniform and gradient errors below 1/j for a cutoff equal to one there. This proves local uniform closure without flattening unbounded presentations or a global uncountable family of seminorms. Positivity survives distributional limits. Minimality puts every stage of P in this sheaf; its span contains continuous dpsh functions. Finite patching on compact X yields
 ∫f DD(gT)=∫g DD(fT)=-Q_T(f,g), Q_T(f,f)≥0.

Define E(0)=0 and E(u)=⅓∫u[MA(0)+B(u,0)+MA(u)]. For u_t=(1-t)u+tv, differentiation of this cubic and Green with T=θ,θ_{u_t} give
 dE(u_t)/dt=∫(v-u)MA(u_t),
 d²E(u_t)/dt²=-2Q_{θ_{u_t}}(v-u,v-u)≤0.
Thus E is monotone, concave, satisfies E(u+c)=E(u)+Mc, and obeys the tangent inequality. Integrating the quadratic Bernstein coefficients gives
 E(u)-E(v)=⅓∫(u-v)[MA(u)+B(u,v)+MA(v)].
For u≥v, each nonnegative integral is at most 3(E(u)-E(v)). Bounded comparison follows from max(u,v-ε), locality and common mass:
 MA(v){u<v-ε}≤MA(u){u≤v-ε}.
Letting ε decrease to zero gives MA(v){u<v}≤MA(u){u<v}, retaining contact atoms at the intermediate stage.

Define G to consist of actual pointwise functions u_j↓u with u_j∈C and inf E(u_j)>-∞. These are upper-semicontinuous local CLD-generated psh potentials. Indeed the sheaf generated by smooth psh functions and decreasing limits is closed under uniform limits with finite continuous limit: if |f_j-f|≤ε_j, pass to ε_{j+1}<ε_j/3, and f_j+2ε_j decreases to f. Zero errors allow a constant subsequence. Hence its continuous part contains P by minimality, and ρ+u_j↓ρ+u belongs to that decreasing sheaf. This does not establish higher-dimensional classical curve-test recognition or all intrinsic unbounded psh membership.

Energy is canonical for EVERY bounded continuous decreasing presentation. If v_k↓u and continuous a satisfies u<a everywhere, the increasing open sets {v_k<a} cover compact X, so one index works everywhere. Apply this with a=u_j+ε and reverse the two presentations. Monotonicity and the constant rule equate their energy limits and establish finiteness of the second presentation. The same argument proves order preservation. An identically -∞ limit eventually lies below every constant -A, contradicting the energy bound.

Finite convex combinations belong to G by concavity. Energy on each finite simplex is a polynomial of degree at most three. Bounded polynomial values converge at a finite unisolvent interpolation set inside the simplex; coefficients therefore converge. The resulting polynomial equals canonical energy at every simplex point. Such interpolation sets exist because a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on an open simplex. Endpoints omit zero-weight functions, avoiding 0·(-∞).

The exact continuity statement is restricted: if u_k∈G decrease to u ALREADY IN G, then E(u_k)↓E(u). For a continuous presentation term v_l of u, the increasing open sets {u_k<v_l+ε} cover X because u_k is upper semicontinuous. Order preservation followed by l→∞ and ε→0 proves the claim. It does not prove generation of an arbitrary limit, net closure or global diagonal flattening.

For a positive finite Radon measure define E*(μ)=sup_{v∈C}(E(v)-∫v dμ). Constants force μ(X)=M when E*(μ)<∞. Shift a presentation below zero, apply its bounded dual inequality, and use monotone convergence; the shift cancels by mass M. For every u∈G this proves integrability, nullity of its pole set, and
 ∫(-u)dμ≤E*(μ)-E(u) for u≤0,
 ∫|u_j-u|dμ→0.
Bounded tangent gives E*(MA(v))=E(v)-∫v MA(v) for v∈C.

notes.summary: Independent all-direction generated analytic MA/mixed operator, finite moments, comparison and exact mass-two clamps.
notes.detailedSummary: Cubic boundary coefficients and dense continuous tests determine presentation-independent weak limits of genuine analytic bounded products. Proves finite full dual, self moments, generated first variation, moving L1 estimates, comparison on nonopen sets, mixed locality and strict contact-excluding clamps with explicit tails. The domain is generated; arbitrary intrinsic products and arbitrary-measure existence are not established.
notes.text:
Use the carrier and dense test lattice of n1 and the independent bounded calculus and generated energy of n2. The domain is precisely G, the actual decreasing limits of bounded continuous members of the ALL-stage minimal continuous sheaf with finite canonical energy. No invariance, radiality or measure-support restriction is imposed. This does not recognize every intrinsic unbounded psh function or prove an arbitrary-measure equation theorem.

For EVERY presentation u_j↓u∈G and fixed v∈C, put P_j(t)=E((1-t)u_j+tv), R_j(t)=E(tu_j). Their degree-at-most-three coefficients converge by finite interpolation of canonical energies. The exact boundary identity is
 ∫v MA(u_j)=P′_j(0)+R′_j(1).
The first derivative integrates v-u_j and the second integrates u_j. Hence the limit depends only on u,v. By linearity it exists on D=span C. For continuous φ choose f∈D with ||φ-f||<η. Positivity and mass M give
 |∫φ(MA(u_j)-MA(u_k))|≤2Mη+|∫f(MA(u_j)-MA(u_k))|.
All continuous-test integrals consequently converge, independently of presentation. Their limit is a positive functional of mass M. Compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation—positive functionals on C(X,R) correspond uniquely to finite regular Borel measures, with mass their value at 1—gives a unique positive Radon MA(u) of raw mass two. It is a weak limit of genuine analytic bounded products, not an inverse measure assigned through a dual definition.

The bounded polarization identity
 B(u_j,v_j)=2MA((u_j+v_j)/2)-½(MA(u_j)+MA(v_j))
gives presentation-independent mixed limits B(u,v), positive of mass M. Averages are generated and positivity passes from bounded measures. Where the limiting local weights are continuous, Dini's compact-cover argument gives uniform convergence on compact subsets; CLD 8.7.2 identifies the limits there with ordinary continuous products. Bounded discontinuity alone does not license that identification.

Let D_u=lim_j∫u_j MA(u_j)=R′(1), a finite polynomial coefficient. Bounded tangent and continuous-test weak convergence give
 E(v)-∫v MA(u)≤E(u)-D_u for v∈C.
Thus E*(MA(u))<∞, and n2 makes EVERY generated potential integrable for MA(u), with generated pole sets null. For k≥j, the bounded cocycle gives
 0≤∫(u_j-u_k)MA(u_k)≤3(E(u_j)-E(u_k)).
Let k→∞ using the fixed continuous test u_j and the already known self-moment limit, then j→∞ using L1(MA(u)). This proves D_u=∫u MA(u). Testing u_j in the dual supplies the reverse bound, so
 E*(MA(u))=E(u)-∫u MA(u).
No unbounded moment was assumed to obtain finite dual.

For u,w∈G, the canonical polynomial F(t,s)=E(tu+sw), on t,s≥0, t+s≤1, satisfies ∂_sF(1,0)=∫w MA(u). First prove this for bounded w by presentations of u and coefficient convergence. For general w take w_l∈C decreasing to it. At every simplex point, tu+sw_l decreases to the ALREADY generated tu+sw. The restricted decreasing-energy continuity of n2 and finite interpolation give coefficient convergence. Finite dual of MA(u) gives L1 convergence in the test slot. This proves the boundary derivative without flattening nested presentations. Zero-weight terms are omitted.

Substitution of a segment into the multivariate energy polynomial, together with this moment formula, gives genuine generated first variation:
 dE((1-t)u+tv)/dt=∫(v-u)MA((1-t)u+tv).
All integrals are finite. Common poles are null, so values of differences there are irrelevant. Concavity passes from bounded polynomials and gives the generated tangent inequality.

If generated u_j,v_j decrease to u,v already in G, energy at every finite convex combination converges by n2; interpolation gives coefficient convergence. Bounded-test moments give weak MA convergence on D, and density plus common mass extends it to all C(X). Polarization gives mixed convergence. The coefficient of E(tu_j+sv_j) gives ∫u_j MA(v_j)→∫u MA(v). Keeping u fixed gives ∫u MA(v_j)→∫u MA(v). Therefore
 ∫|u_j-u|MA(v_j)→0.
Pole sets are null and the difference is nonnegative almost everywhere. Mixed moments have the same limits by polarization; alternatively 0≤B(a,b)≤2MA((a+b)/2) gives integrability and null poles for mixed measures.

Moving moments pass bounded cocycles term by term, giving finite-integral identities
 E(u)=⅓∫u[MA(0)+B(u,0)+MA(u)],
 E(u)-E(v)=⅓∫(u-v)[MA(u)+B(u,v)+MA(v)].
No infinite integrals are subtracted. For u≤0, -∫u MA(u)≤-3E(u), hence E*(MA(u))≤-2E(u).

The indicator argument for comparison requires more than weak convergence. Suppose μ_j→μ weakly have common positive mass; a_j,b_j∈C decrease to generated a,b; their moving L1(μ_j) errors tend to zero; and, for every fixed l, ∫(a_l-a)dμ_j→∫(a_l-a)dμ, likewise for b. These hypotheses hold for μ_j=MA(c_j), c_j↓c∈G, by the preceding moments, and also for mixed measures. The fixed-l limits tend to zero as l→∞.

For bounded Lipschitz H and continuous φ, replace a_j-b_j by a-b using moving L1; replace that by continuous a_l-b_l using fixed-l estimates; use weak convergence at fixed l; finally let l→∞. Thus ∫φH(a_j-b_j)dμ_j→∫φH(a-b)dμ. At any ε with μ{a-b=ε}=0, Lipschitz ramps sandwich the indicator of {a-b>ε}. The limiting gap is bounded by ||φ|| μ{|a-b-ε|≤δ} and tends to zero. Hence strict-indicator convergence holds at atom-free levels. Finite measures have at most countably many positive-mass levels.

Apply bounded comparison to u_j,v_j-ε and use this lemma separately for MA(u_j),MA(v_j). At common atom-free positive levels it passes to {v-u>ε}. Let these levels decrease to zero, proving
 MA(v){u<v}≤MA(u){u<v} for u,v∈G.
For w_j=max(u_j,v_j), monotonicity makes w=max(u,v) generated. Bounded locality on the ordinary open sets {u_j-v_j>ε} and the same indicator passage give
 1_{u>v}MA(max(u,v))=1_{u>v}MA(u).
The limiting set need not be open. Equality first holds against continuous tests and then for restricted measures: finite Borel restrictions of finite regular measures on compact Hausdorff X are regular, so Riesz uniqueness applies. Polarize the identity for (u+z)/2,(v+z)/2 to obtain mixed maximum locality with B(max(u,v),z),B(u,z). Poles of z are null by domination with the finite-dual MA of an average.

For u≤0, u^A=max(u,-A) is generated by max(u_j,-A) and monotonicity. Generated energy and weak continuity apply as A→∞. Maximum locality gives the exact formula
 1_{u>-A}MA(u^A)=1_{u>-A}MA(u).
These measures increase to MA(u), of raw mass two. The ENTIRE contact set {u=-A} is excluded. If E(u)≥-C, finite dual of MA(u^A) and n2 give ∫(-u)MA(u^A)≤3C, hence MA(u^A){u≤-A}≤3C/A.

For u,v≤0 successive mixed locality gives
 1_{u>-A,v>-B}B(u^A,v^B)=1_{u>-A,v>-B}B(u,v).
The mass increases to two. If E(u)≥-C_u and E(v)≥-C_v, domination by 2MA((u^A+v^B)/2), whose dual is at most C_u+C_v, bounds discarded mass by
 2(2C_u+C_v)/A+2(C_u+2C_v)/B.
All contact atoms are on the discarded side.

This independently reconstructs the generated-operator claims of whole393 with explicit source, presentation and locality qualifications. It constructs analytic bounded-limit products and generated clamp products, but does not recognize arbitrary local intrinsic pluripolar sets. Discontinuous generated clamps are not silently called previously defined continuous CLD products. Artifacts: n3.md, scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md. This is scoped progress, not original P16.7 closure.

notes.summary: New all-test strictness estimate Q_theta_w(a-b)≤I/2+sqrt(42CI); equal generated MA implies vanishing bounded gradients. Pointwise uniqueness remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Derives the signed transgression identity from mixed Green, bounds each current-slot energy by 21C, and proves an all-test surface I-estimate without strict background positivity. Moving moments force I_j→0 for equal generated measures. For bounded continuous solutions, capped logs and Poincaré–Lelong yield DD((u-v)δ_divP)=0 locally. Unbounded divisor restriction and the remaining separation bridge are not proved.
notes.text:
This is a new advance using n1–n3, without asserting that θ is strictly positive. For bounded continuous dpsh f,h and positive closed T write Q_T(f,h)=-∫f DD(hT), with the Hilbert interpretation from n2. Extend to differences of positive closed currents by linearity.

For a,b,w∈C put f=a-b, g=(a+b)/2, h=w-g and I(a,b)=∫(a-b)[MA(b)-MA(a)]. Product expansion and Green give
 I(a,b)=Q_{θ_a}(f,f)+Q_{θ_b}(f,f)≥0.
The exact transgression, including its sign, is
 Q_{θ_w}(f,f)-Q_{θ_g}(f,f)=Q_{θ_a}(f,h)-Q_{θ_b}(f,h).
Indeed the left side is -∫f DDf∧DDh by the recursive dpsh rule. Symmetry makes it -∫f DDh∧DDf=Q_{DDf}(f,h), the right side because DDf=θ_a-θ_b. Arbitrary continuous coefficients are not declared closed, and no global Hessian domination is used. Cauchy–Schwarz yields
 Q_{θ_w}(f,f)≤I(a,b)/2+sqrt(I(a,b)(Q_{θ_a}(h,h)+Q_{θ_b}(h,h))).

Normalize a,b,w≤0 by individual constants and suppose their energies are ≥-C, C≥0. Constants change neither gradients nor I. The dual estimate of n3 gives ∫(-p)MA(q)≤3C for these potentials. Also B(q,r)≤2MA((q+r)/2); concavity and the dual estimate give ∫(-p)B(q,r)≤6C. Since |h|≤-w+(-a-b)/2,
 ∫|h|MA(q)≤6C, ∫|h|B(q,r)≤12C.
Finally
 Q_{θ_a}(h,h)=-∫h[B(a,w)-(MA(a)+B(a,b))/2]≤21C,
and similarly for b. The arithmetic is 12C+3C+6C=21C in each slot. Thus
 Q_{θ_w}(a-b,a-b)≤I(a,b)/2+sqrt(42C I(a,b)).
This is a proved bounded surface I-estimate for arbitrary bounded θ-psh tests, not an assumed CLN bridge.

If u,v∈G and MA(u)=MA(v), take ANY bounded continuous decreasing presentations u_j,v_j. Subtract fixed upper bounds from the presentations and normalize fixed w∈C below zero. Their energies have a common lower bound -C. All four terms of
 I_j=∫u_j MA(v_j)-∫v_j MA(v_j)-∫u_j MA(u_j)+∫v_j MA(u_j)
converge by n3. Equality of the limiting measures gives I_j→0; bounded positivity gives I_j≥0. Consequently
 Q_{θ_w}(u_j-v_j,u_j-v_j)→0
for EVERY fixed bounded w. This is independent of both presentations. It is convergence of actual bounded gradients, not a definition of a gradient for an arbitrary discontinuous difference.

There is a local analytic consequence for bounded continuous solutions. For u,v∈C with equal MA the estimate gives Q_{θ_w}(u-v,u-v)=0 for every w∈C. Green and Cauchy–Schwarz against compact smooth scalar tests yield DD((u-v)θ_w)=0.

This detects local divisors despite θ vanishing on residue bidiscs. Let P be a nonzero Laurent polynomial and choose a lift chart |x_i-a_i|<r centered at the tropical class of a point of its zero locus. Choose smooth convex χ:R→R with χ=0 on (-∞,0], 0≤χ′≤1, and χ(t)=t-c for t≥1. Set ψ_N=χ(log|P|+N), extending it by zero near its zeros. It is ordinary smooth psh: near a zero it is constant; elsewhere it is a convex smooth function of a unit moment.

Choose 0<δ<r²/4 and ε_N>0 so δ+ε_N sup ψ_N<r²/2 on the closed chart. Then
 w_N=max(ρ_a,δ+ε_Nψ_N)-ρ_a,
extended by zero, belongs to C by the collar and soft-maximum construction of n1. On the FIXED ordinary neighbourhood {ρ_a<δ/2}, independent of N, θ_{w_N}=ε_N DDψ_N. Therefore DD((u-v)DDψ_N)=0 there for every N.

The further source input is CLD v2 Theorem 16.7.3: for a regular meromorphic function P on a boundaryless pure-dimensional analytic space, DD[log|P|]=δ_divP. Its complete statement and immediate proof, literal LF23468–23656, were read inside the complete LF23458–23671 unit. Its proof uses compact tropical charts, Theorem 14.7.2 boundary-product calibration and Stokes; deeper inputs remain conventional. A smooth torus chart and nonzero holomorphic P satisfy regularity. The proof explains why compact smooth top-test supports avoid the lower-dimensional zero locus. Consequently [ψ_N-N]→[log|P|-c] on those tests, eventually exactly, and DDψ_N→δ_divP as positive currents. CLD 8.5.1 permits multiplication by the bounded continuous u-v; differentiation then gives the genuine local identity
 DD((u-v)δ_divP)=0.
This is an analytic divisor-current consequence. Bounded continuity is essential: multiplication through this limit has not been justified for unbounded generated differences.

The remaining uniqueness gap is explicit. These vanishing gradients/current tests have not been shown to force actual pointwise generated potentials to differ by a constant. Q_θ=0 alone cannot give that conclusion. Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, assumes an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field and continuous functions on open subsets of smooth algebraic curves. K=C((s)) is not algebraically closed. Her theorem cannot be applied directly here; even a justified field change would leave an unbounded restriction/integrability problem. One positive Hessian current also does not establish higher-dimensional classical psh recognition.

Artifacts: n4.md, scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md contain the full strictness and divisor arguments. They are partial progress, not full uniqueness or P16.7 closure.

The missing original equation gate is exact. For generated solutions n3 proves
 μ=MA(u) ⇒ μ(X)=2 and E*(μ)=E(u)-∫u dμ<∞.
For a measure with finite bounded dual, the supremum over the whole generated domain equals the bounded dual: every generated potential is integrable and its bounded presentation passes the objective to the limit. This is a noncircular necessary condition allowing arbitrary support. It does not prove that every positive Radon measure of mass two and finite full bounded dual belongs to the image of MA.

Variational maximization of E(u)-∫u dμ is well-defined on G for such μ, but no separated compact topology on normalized energy sublevels has been proved that represents maximizing limits by actual generated potentials. The estimate ∫(-u)dμ≤E*(μ)+C is only an L1 bound; it supplies neither uniform integrability nor separation nor closure/generation of limits. Density of bounded potential tests in C(X) proves measure convergence, not function-space compactness. Neither a sequence-to-net substitution nor unjustified diagonal flattening closes this gap.

The upper envelope of bounded potentials under an arbitrary continuous obstacle is also not proved to be an actual continuous analytic psh potential with orthogonality. Finite max closure does not establish this infinite-envelope regularity. No complete replacement variation argument identifies a maximizer’s measure with every prescribed eligible measure without the missing representability/variation gate. Defining eligibility as already being MA(u) would be circular and is not done.

For uniqueness, n4 proves I_j→0 and vanishing bounded gradient norms against every bounded test when limiting measures agree. The remaining domination/separation or removable-singularity/curve-recognition argument identifying actual pointwise generated potentials modulo constants is unproved. Divisor-current multiplication is established only for bounded continuous differences. The degenerate background does not force constants by itself.

Original P16.7 remains unresolved. Its precise residual is: intrinsic E1 recognition or a complete justified analytic completion with actual representatives; closure and separated normalized energy-sublevel compactness; continuous analytic obstacle envelopes and orthogonality or fully proved replacements; existence for EVERY eligible arbitrary-support positive Radon measure of the fixed mass under a noncircular sufficient finite-energy condition; and full uniqueness modulo constants. Arbitrary intrinsic bounded-discontinuous products and general local pluripolar recognition also remain outside the generated theorem. No analytic counterexample to the original axis or to finite-full-dual sufficiency was proved.
